tone_statements.citation: Dunstan, Margaret Elizabeth. 1966. Tone and concord systems in Ngwe nominals. PhD thesis, University of London (SOAS), 336 pp.
tone_statements.quote: These disyllabic nouns fall into three tonal classes and these tonal classes cut across the noun class system … In citation form, tone class 1 has a low-tone prefix followed by a low-tone stem … Before pause the low-tone stem is realised as a low fall. In citation form, tone class TT has a low-tone prefix followed by a high-tone stem … In citation form, tone class III has a high-tone prefix followed by a high-tone stem, but in any longer utterance the stem is realised as low-tone. … high tone is lower in pitch than the preceding one, whether intervening low tones occur or not.
tone_statements.locator: p. 33, opening paragraphs and the note before Example 1 (summary table and P-rules on pp. 36-38)
tone_statements.summary: Prefix and stem syllables of nouns each carry high or low tone (three tonal classes of disyllabic nouns); prefix tones alternate by syntactic position; successive highs step down; falls derived.

tone.quote: The Nweh Alphabet has over 34 letters as compared to the 26 letters of the English Alphabet. Because Nweh is a tonal language, there are some letters that need to capture the nasal sounds in the language. The Nweh Alphabet is based off the General Alphabet of Cameroon, an orthographic system created in the late 1970s for all Cameroonian languages, and once you master the Alphabet, reading in Nweh and other languages will be much easier.
